message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to lock my roommate and her friend out of our dorm room. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We live in a dorm room with two beds and desks, pretty standard. My roommate and her friend have started doing this thing that's really annoying. Whenever my boyfriend and I are in our room, and they leave, they leave the door wide open. They laugh and say "this is what you get" as if it's for showing minimal PDAs with my boyfriend in my room. But honestly, we're just watching Netflix in my bed, nothing more. I feel like they're invading my privacy, and they're doing it on purpose to make me feel uncomfortable. Tonight, they left the room giggling and said "good luck" as they left the door open. They do this going in and out of the room like five times an hour. Each time, I get up and close the door. I got sick of it on their sixth trip, so I just locked the door. I know she has the key, but if I have to go through the hassle of getting up to close the door, they can go through the hassle of unlocking it. Then, the friend comes for their seventh trip and can't open the door and starts banging like crazy. I don't open the door because she knew what she was doing. She went back wherever she and my roommate were hanging out and got the key and came in. Then she told me it was very rude that I locked the door because "it's my roommate's room." I calmly said, "If you're going to make me get up and close the door, you can go through the process of unlocking it." My boyfriend also asked why they were acting so passive-aggressive for no reason. She laughed and called me disrespectful again and left, leaving the door wide open. Am I really the asshole for just wanting my door kept closed so everyone passing by doesn't see me in my bed? Okay, so I need to figure out if it's right or wrong for me to lock them out. Let's break this down. First, the issue is about privacy. I feel like my privacy is being invaded when they leave the door open intentionally. They're doing it to make me feel uncomfortable, which is not cool. On the other hand, they might feel like they have the right to leave the door open because it's their room too. I locked the door because I was tired of getting up to close it every time they left. I thought, if they can't be responsible about closing the door, I can take the step to lock it. But then, when they tried to get in and couldn't, they got angry and called me rude and disrespectful. Is it reasonable for me to want privacy in my own room? I think so. But is locking them out the right way to handle it? Maybe not. It seems like it escalated the situation. Perhaps there's a better way to communicate my feelings without locking them out. Maybe talking to them calmly about how their actions are making me uncomfortable and asking them to close the door when they leave. If they continue to do it intentionally, maybe there are other steps I can take, like involving a dorm advisor or something. Locking them out might have made them feel like I'm being unreasonable, especially since they have a key. It's a shared space, so both parties should respect each other's needs. In the end, I think it's not entirely wrong to want privacy, but the way I handled it by locking them out might have been a bit harsh. Communication seems like a better approach to resolve this conflict.
